BiblicalUsage: Agam means to be grieved, and it appears only once — in Job's defence of his life: 'Did not I weep for him that was in trouble? was not my soul grieved for the poor?' Job is answering his friends by pointing to the compassion of his past: he wept with the troubled and grieved for the needy, and that grief was the mark of a righteous man.
TheologicalSignificance: On its own it is too small to build on, and I would rather read it honestly in its verse than make it mean more than it does; in this case, the verse is Job 30:25.
